newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares open weaker on move to undervalueds.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares open weaker on move to undervalueds.

text.p: Leading Russian shares opened weaker on Friday as investors moved funds from liquid stocks into those deemed undervalued, and traders anticipated a slight correction.

"Everybody is talking about a correction of 5-10 percent," said Creditanstalt sales director Tad Berger, predicting leading shares would weaken gradually on Friday and over the next week but would find support after a short fall.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened at 501.62, slightly off its 502.48 Thursday close.
National power company UES, the most-traded share by dollar volume, ticked down to $0.4500 at 0820 GMT from $0.4505.

Traders said investors were seeking out regional telecoms and utilities. A few mentioned the metals and pipe-manufacturing sectors, which have long been ignored but are now seen as potential buys as the economy recovers and infrastructure needs increase.
Nizhnetagilsk steel maker rose strongly to $0.175 from $0.160. Izhorskie Zavody heavy equipment maker rose to $68.00 from $67.00 on a single trade.
One Moscow trader saw the the leading half-dozen shares weakening and correcting after a week or so as Western investors who have been in the market reallocate funds.
New funds are still flowing into the market. But they are doing so at a much lower volume than earlier in this bull market phase which began about a month ago when the RTS index was near 360.
Russian operators were not seen strongly affecting the market, which is being steadied by long-term foreign investors.
